# SQL OR Operator

#### Course: Learn SQL Basics

## SQL OR Operator

The OR operator is used in the WHERE clause to combine multiple conditions. A row is included in the results if at least one condition is TRUE.

Imagine you want to find customers younger than 23 or older than 27.

This requires two conditions, and only one needs to be true:

- The customer's age can be less than 23.
- The customer's age can be greater than 27.

Here's how you can combine these conditions using the OR operator:

```sql
1-- Select rows where age is either less than 23 or greater than 27
2
3SELECT first_name, age  
4FROM Customers  
5WHERE age < 23 OR age > 27;
```

Here's how this query works:

![Working of the OR operator](data:image/png;base64,)

The OR operator ensures that a row is included in the results if either condition (age < 23 or age > 27) is true. Customers will appear in the output if they meet one or both conditions.
